note: The reported symptom IS this diagnostic, quoted verbatim from the issue body, so it is written in literally rather than approximated. Two reasons this exact string and not a looser pattern: (1) `no member named` is one of classify()'s feature-absence markers, and the demotion is suppressed only when a POSITIVE clause of this predicate quotes the matched marker verbatim -- an approximation would let every reproducing probe be demoted to invalid-probe (the #3055 trap, in the direction where it discards evidence); (2) it is self-anchoring against vacuity: the compiler can only name 'StructuredBuffer<float>' as the object type if it parsed the shader, accepted ResourceDescriptorHeap, resolved the cast, and reached member lookup -- so a build that predates SM 6.6 cannot produce it, and neither can a run that failed to parse. A build lacking ResourceDescriptorHeap instead answers 'use of undeclared identifier', which this predicate does not quote, so such probes are still correctly demoted. This is a presence predicate, not an absence one, so the failed-parse-scores-as-repro hazard does not apply. Controls: control-local.hlsl (the maintainer's documented workaround, --expect no-match) proves the predicate does not fire on a correct shader that uses the same feature; control-heap.hlsl (--expect no-match) is the feature-presence probe that separates 'this release predates SM 6.6' from 'this release rejected something else'.
